subject: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality comparisons & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karen Liu <karen.liu@nimbus.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive eval follow-up: model quality comparisons & next tests

Hi Karen — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary objective: determine whether Redwood can match or improve on Nimbus' current inference costs while maintaining or improving model quality for long-form, multi-turn QA and product-description generation.
- Top concerns: hallucination rate on long-form answers, formatting/structured output, latency during peak traffic, and integration with your existing pipeline for re-ranking.

Where Redwood shines (short list)
- Model routing + fallback: can route live traffic to lower-cost quantized model variants and fall back to full-precision variants on critical paths.
- Cost controls: token-level cost visibility and per-route batching/caching knobs to reduce unit cost without regressing output quality.
- Quality monitoring: built-in eval harness to run repeatable prompt sets and detect regressions (hallucination detection included).

Proposed next tests (we can run these on hosted Redwood endpoints or provide configs if you prefer to run in your environment):
1) Long-form QA: 150 prompts (context up to 8k tokens) — measure hallucination rate, factuality checks vs gold, and EM/ROUGE.
2) Instruction-following & structure: 100 prompts requiring JSON/CSV outputs — measure exact-match & parsing errors.
3) Multi-turn conversational consistency: 200 sessions — track context carryover errors and token-latency (p50/p95).

Deliverables and timeline
- Today: I attach eval_config.csv with the proposed test mix and eval_prompts.txt with sample prompts.
- By Fri (2026-08-28): we’ll run a first-pass comparison against your current hyperscaler baseline and share baseline_results_summary.pdf with per-test metrics.
- Follow-up call: propose Mon 2026-08-31 to review results and decide whether to run a larger production trial.

Ask: please confirm whether we should run the tests on Redwood-hosted endpoints or provide you the config to run in your environment, and whether Procurement should be looped for any contractual trial terms.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eval_config.csv, eval_prompts.txt

From: Karen Liu <karen.liu@nimbus.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbus.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Competitive eval-follow-up: model quality comparisons & next tests

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications before we proceed:

1) Can you confirm the exact metric you use for hallucination rate? We need a clear definition we can reconcile with our internal checks.
2) For long-form QA, we need to preserve citations/traceability where possible — will Redwood’s outputs flag source chunks or confidence scores?
3) Are the eval_prompts you attached obfuscated (no PII)? We have strict data handling requirements.

We prefer Redwood to run the initial baseline against our public benchmark set (we'll provide a link to the dataset next). If results look promising, Procurement will request a short trial contract for Dedicated capacity (1 GPU pool) to run larger-scale tests.

Also: timeline-wise, we need the first summary by EOD Fri 2026-08-28 as you proposed.

—Karen
VP, Product
Nimbus AI

Thanks for the quick reply, Karen — answers inline and next steps below.

1) Hallucination definition: we use a precision-oriented check — the hallucination rate is the percent of generated claims (spans of output that assert facts) that do not match any evidence in the provided context or the agreed ground-truth. We provide span-level annotations and a "confidence score" heuristic. We'll include the exact matcher we use so Nimbus can run the same check.

2) Citations/traceability: for long-form QA we enable token-level provenance when we run with provided context (we return source chunk ids and optionally a confidence score per claim). If you need stricter provenance (signed references), we can discuss instrumenting your pipeline for deterministic chunk IDs.

3) Data handling: all eval prompts are scrubbed of customer PII. If you want us to run against your internal dataset in a private deployment, we can provide an NDA and run in a Private environment or a dedicated trial.

Next steps (to meet the EOD Fri deliverable):
- We will run the 3 short tests on Redwood-hosted endpoints against the public benchmark you share.
- Deliver baseline_results_summary.pdf by Friday with per-test: hallucination rate, EM/ROUGE, parsing errors for structured outputs, p50/p95 latency, and token-cost delta vs your current provider.

I've attached eval_prompts.txt — highlights: long-form QA prompts that include multi-paragraph contexts; JSON-output structural prompts (for product descriptions); and multi-turn dialog seeds.

If that works, we'll proceed and loop Procurement for trial contract language if the first pass looks good.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: eval_prompts.txt

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed eval prompts & metrics (for Nimbus baseline run)

Internal notes — planned prompts/metrics to include in the Friday run (this is the set I used on recent competitive evals):

Eval buckets and sample metrics:
- Long-form QA (150 items): hallucination_rate (span-level), EM, ROUGE-L, answer_length, cite_coverage (percent of claims backed by context).
- Structured output (100 items): exact_match(JSON schema), parse_error_rate, field_level_precision/recall.
- Multi-turn context (200 sessions): consistency_error_rate (contradictory facts across turns), context_utilization (% of tokens from prior turns used), latency_p50/p95.
- Safety/prompt-injection checks (50 items): unsafe_response_rate, instruction-following fidelity.

Thresholds we should flag: hallucination_rate > 5% on long-form, parse_error_rate > 3% for structured outputs, latency_p95 > 800ms on target GPU config.

Implementation details:
- Use same seed tokens and deterministic decoding where possible for repeatability.
- Compare Redwood-hosted quantized model variant, full-precision variant, and Nimbus' current hyperscaler model (we'll ask Nimbus to provide a baseline result file or allow Redwood to pull from their public benchmark link).
- Produce an artifacts bundle: per-prompt output CSV, per-model metrics summary, and a short deck with examples (good / bad) for the customer call.

I'll run the baseline harness and drop results into the Drive folder linked above. Marissa — I recommend we highlight 3 example hallucinations and 3 structured-output failures in the Friday deck to give Nimbus concrete examples.

-Neha
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
